definitions.explanation: A region in which a force operates.

examples.japanese: その{場|ば}を{離|はな}れた。
その{場|ば}で{決|き}めましょう。
{話|はな}し{合|あ}いの{場|ば}を{設|もう}けた。
examples.english: We set up a venue for discussion.
examples.notes: {場|ば}を{設|もう}ける = to set up a venue/forum

examples.japanese: {場|ば}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: To read the atmosphere of the situation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{冗談|じょうだん}で{場|ば}が{白|しら}けてしまった。
examples.english: His joke made the mood go flat.
examples.notes: {場|ば}が{白|しら}ける = the mood becomes awkward/flat

examples.japanese: {磁場|じば}の{強|つよ}さを{測定|そくてい}する。
examples.english: To measure the strength of a magnetic field.

examples.japanese: {重力場|じゅうりょくば}の{中|なか}では{物体|ぶったい}は{落下|らっか}する。
examples.english: Objects fall within a gravitational field.
examples.notes: {重力場|じゅうりょくば} = gravitational field

examples.japanese: {電磁場|でんじば}の{理論|りろん}は{物理学|ぶつりがく}の{重要|じゅうよう}な{分野|ぶんや}だ。
examples.english: The theory of electromagnetic fields is an important area of physics.

notes:
Used independently or as a suffix. Often relates to social situations and atmosphere.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{場|ば}を{読|よ}む (to read the room/situation)
・その{場|ば}で (on the spot)
・{場|ば}を{盛|も}り{上|あ}げる (to liven things up)
・{場|ば}が{白|しら}ける (the mood becomes awkward)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{場所|ばしょ} (place, location)
・{場面|ばめん} (scene)
・{場合|ばあい} (case, situation)
・{現場|げんば} (actual site, scene)
・{磁場|じば} (magnetic field)

NOTE:
・When read as {場|ば}, often refers to social/situational context
・In compounds, both ば and じょう readings occur
